intro:
Use it to compare categories by length: revenue per month, messages per channel. Each row of `data` is a band, and each `BarChart.Bar` is a series drawn from one of its keys.

The grid, the axes, the legend and the readout are separate parts, so a chart has only the ones you write.

The value axis always includes zero, because a bar cropped at the bottom misstates its value. For a series where the change matters more than the size, use a line chart instead.

parts.Header: The strip above the plot: `title`, `value` and `caption`, with the series key or your own control on the trailing side.
parts.Grid: Lines across the value axis, in the theme's border colour. `rows` is roughly how many: the axis picks round numbers near it.
parts.Bar: One series. Declare one per key. Their order is the order they stand in a band, and from the baseline up in a stack.
parts.Skeleton: A row of short, equal stubs on the baseline with a highlight moving across them, drawn only while `status` is `loading`.
parts.XAxis: Category labels under the bands. Labels are dropped when the bands are too narrow to fit them. Draws nothing on a horizontal chart.
parts.YAxis: Value labels on the grid lines, in round numbers, with room made for them. On a horizontal chart it draws the category names instead.
parts.Legend: A swatch and a name per series, over the top corner of the plot. On a chart with a header, use the header's `legend` prop instead.
parts.Tooltip: The readout, and what drives it. It covers the plot, so the pointer does not have to land on a bar. `labels` names the series in it.

examples.title: Two series side by side
examples.description: Declare a `Bar` per series. They share the width `barGap` leaves in each band. `color` names one of the theme's roles.

examples.title: Stacked
examples.description: `stacked` adds the series into a total, so give it series that add up, such as costs and profit. `stackGap` leaves a hairline between the segments, which keeps similar colours apart. The first `Bar` is the lowest segment.

examples.title: Sideways
examples.description: Use `orientation="horizontal"` when the category names are longer than a band is wide. `YAxis` draws the names down the side.

examples.title: Values too small to see
examples.description: `minBarLength` draws any non-zero bar at a visible length. Thursday's zero still draws nothing.

examples.title: Dot matrix
examples.description:
`texture="dots"` fills the bars with a grid of dots instead of a solid colour. The dots are brightest towards the end a bar grows to, measured across the whole plot, so a taller bar reaches brighter dots. Every bar shares one grid, so the rows of dots line up across the chart.

`dotSize` and `dotGap` set the grid, in pixels. Square bars with `cornerRadius={0}` keep the edge of the grid clean, and `font-mono uppercase` on the chart sets its axes in a readout's type.

examples.title: Loading, then data
examples.description: Add `BarChart.Skeleton` and drive `status`. The bars grow out of the baseline when it turns `ready`. It draws one stub per row, or seven with no rows yet; `bars` sets another count.

examples.title: Changing data
examples.description: When `data` changes, the bars and the axis move to their new values over `domainDuration`, and a bar under the same band and series keeps its identity. A `ref` on the chart has `replay()`, which grows the bars in again.

notes:
### Sizing

The chart fills its container's width and takes its height from `aspectRatio`, which applies to the plot alone, so a header does not shrink it. The plot draws in the browser after it has been measured, and the space is reserved until then, so it is not in server-rendered HTML.

### Bundle size

The chart adds about 60 KB of gzipped JavaScript to a page that uses it. A page that does not import it pays nothing, including one that imports other components from the package root.

### Colour

`color` on `BarChart.Bar` names a role in the theme. Every series defaults to `chart-1`, so give the others their own.

### Reading a band

With a `Tooltip`, hovering a band reads it. A click or a tap pins the reading until the next press elsewhere, or Escape. On a touch screen a sideways drag reads the bands it crosses, and a vertical drag scrolls the page.

`onActiveIndexChange` fires when the band changes, not on every frame, so it can drive a readout outside the chart, as the first example does. Inside the chart, `useBarChart` gives the same band.

### Keyboard

With a `Tooltip`, the plot takes focus. The arrow keys move between bands, Home and End go to the first and last, Enter or Space pins the reading, and Escape clears it.

### Screen readers

Each row is given as text beside the drawing. `label` names the chart and `labelForDatum` writes a row, for values with a unit. Without them a row is read as its keys and values.

### Reduced motion

With reduced motion set, the bars and the axis appear at their final values, and the skeleton's highlight is not drawn.
propsNote: `BarChart`, `BarChart.Header` and `BarChart.Legend` also take the props of the element they render, and a `className`. `BarChart.Tooltip` puts its `className` on the readout. The other parts draw nothing themselves and take only the props listed.
